questions.question: How many **‘**factors of production**’ **are there?
questions.solution:
• There are four factors of production, which are land, labour, goods, and entrepreneurship.
 
• In an economy, these factors are responsible for producing goods and services and are the inputs needed for supply.

questions.question: Agriculture comes under which sector of economic activity?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Agriculture comes under the **primary sector** __of economic activity.
 
• The primary sector includes the production and extraction of raw materials.
 
• The other activities which are related to this sector are mining, forestry, grazing, farming, hunting, fishing, quarrying, and gathering.
 
• The other three sectors of the economy include secondary, tertiary, and quaternary.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
• The Vice President of India is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
 
• The current Chairman of Rajya Sabha is Jagdeep Dhankhar.

questions.question: Which among the following is known as the earliest period in history?
questions.solution:
• Palaeolithic age is known as the earliest period in history. It means old stone age when the first use of stone tools began.
 
• Mesolithic age was the middle stone age, which ended with the introduction of agriculture.
 
• Neolithic age was the new stone age where a lot of social development took place.
 
• Chalcolithic age was the copper age where early copper metallurgy appeared.

questions.question: During 1850’s, Britain came to be known as _________.
questions.solution: During 1850’s, Britain came to be known as the workshop of the world since it became the leading industrial nation in the 19th century because of its mechanised manufacturing of cotton textiles and also the growth of its iron and steel industries in the 1850s.

questions.question: The sun, the moon and all those objects shining in the night sky are called as_________.
questions.solution:
• The sun, the moon and all those objects shining in the night sky are called celestial bodies.
 
• These celestial bodies are not visible in the daytime because of the bright light of the sun.
 
• Any natural body outside the Earth’s atmosphere is known as a celestial body.

questions.question: Which imaginary line running on the globe divides it into two equal parts?
questions.solution:
• The equator is an imaginary line that divides the earth into two equal parts, i.e in the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• Tropic of Cancer is the northerly circle of latitude on earth at which the sun gets directly overhead.
 
• Tropic of Capricorn is the southernmost latitude where the sun is directly overhead.

questions.question: Which type of plants have their branches in the upper part of the stem, much above the ground?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Trees.**

__**Explanation-**__

**Shrubs:** Shrubs are medium-sized, woody plants taller than herbs and have multiple stems. However, they are smaller than trees. Their branches grow near the base, close to the ground and are usually dense and bushy. Examples include azaleas and boxwood.

**Trees: **Trees are the largest plants, and they have a single woody stem or trunk that extends a significant distance above the ground before dividing into branches. The branches of trees primarily grow from the upper part of the stem, well above the ground. Mature trees are typically capable of withstanding all seasons. Examples include oak trees, maple trees, and pine trees.

**Herbs:** Herbs are small, non-woody and flowering plants. They complete their life cycle in one or two seasons. The term "herb" is also used to describe plants that have medicinal properties or are used for their flavor or scent. Examples include grasses, wheat, and tulips.

questions.question: Plants with green and tender stems are called as_________.
questions.solution:
• Plants with green and tender stems are called as herbs. Its examples are tomatoes, wheat, etc.
 
• Trees have their branches in the upper part of the stem, much above the ground.
 
• Shrubs have the stem branching out near the base.

questions.question: The covering of lungs is called as ________.
questions.solution:
• The covering of lungs is called the pleural membrane.
 
• It is a shiny, clear, thin covering that covers the lungs.
 
• Its outer parietal layer is attached to the chest wall, while the inner, visceral layer is attached to the lungs.

questions.question: Unit of acceleration is_________.
questions.solution:
• Unit of acceleration is m/s².
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• Acceleration is a vector quantity.
 
• It has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: The distance travelled by a freely falling body is proportional to which among the following?

options.text: The square of the time of fall
The square root of the time of fall

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Velocity of the particle is defined as the rate of change of its displacement and can be expressed as

vec v = frac{{overrightarrow {dx} }}{{dt}}

 
• And acceleration of the particle is defined as the rate of change of its velocity and can be expressed as

vec a = frac{{overrightarrow {dv} }}{{dt}}

 
• Whereas motion of particles can be predicted using Kinematic equations and they are given as
 
• S = ut + (1)/(2)a{t²}
 
• v = u + at
 
• {v²} = {u²} + 2as

Here,

Displacement of particle = S

Initial velocity = u

Final velocity = v

Acceleration of particle = a

Time period at any instant = t

**Explanation:**__

From the above given explanation, we can see that if a body is falling freely under gravity the body will be accelerated towards the ground at the rate of g and it can be expressed as shown below

h = (0)t + (1)/(2)g{t²}

here, displacement is considered as h and initial velocity will be zero since the body was at rest initially

Hence distance travelled by freely falling body is h = (1)/(2)g{t²}

So, the **distance travelled **by a freely falling body is **proportional to the square of the time of fall.**

questions.question:
Which of the following is **NOT** an input device?

I. Keyboard

II. Mouse

III. Monitor
questions.solution:
• An output device is a device which is used for sending data from computer to the user.
 
• For example Monitor, speakers, headphones, and printers.
 
• An input device is a hardware device which is used to send data to a computer.
 
• For example keyboard, mouse, joystick, and scanners.

questions.question: Molecules in Solids______
questions.solution:
• Molecules in solids cannot move because they are closely packed together. Even though they are locked into place, they still can vibrate a little bit.
 
• In liquids, the molecules are less densely packed and can move around and slide past each other easily.
 
• In gases, the molecules are much more spread out and can move freely and vibrate at high speeds.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an element?
questions.solution:
• Water is not an element but a chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
 
• An element is when only a single type of an atom exists in a substance such as carbon, sodium, and tin.
 
• A compound is a substance that is made up of two or more elements.

questions.question: The Upper limit of the layer where all the space between particles of soil and gaps between rocks are filled with water is called what?
questions.solution:
• The Upper limit of the layer where all the space between particles of soil and gaps between rocks are filled with water is called the water table.
 
• Water cycle describes the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the earth.
 
• Groundwater is the water present under the Earth’s surface in the fractures of rock formations and in soil pore spaces.
 
• An aquifer is an underground body of water-bearing permeable rock.

questions.question: Who among the following discovered Radium?
questions.solution:
• Radium was discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898.
 
• Radium was obtained from pitchblende, a material that contains uranium.

questions.question: With which sport is **“wide ball”** associated?
questions.solution:
• Wide ball is associated with cricket.
 
• A wide ball is called when the batsman is unable to reach the ball while playing a normal stroke.
 
• It does not count as one of the six legitimate balls of the bowler in an over.

questions.question: Hindu Pilgrimage centre Sabarimala is located in which state?
questions.solution:
• Hindu Pilgrimage center Sabarimala is located at the Periyar Tiger Reserve in the Western Ghat mountain ranges of Pathanamthitta district, Perunad, Kerala.
 
• It is one of the world’s largest annual pilgrimages with over 40-50 million devotees visiting each year.

questions.question: Who won the Best FIFA Men’s player award 2016?
questions.solution: Cristiano Ronaldo won the Best FIFA Men’s player award 2016, while the Best FIFA Women’s player was won by Carli Lloyd.

questions.question: Basel Convention is an international treaty that was designed__________.

options.text: to reduce movement of hazardous waste (except radioactive wastes) between nations.
to reduce movement of radioactive wastes only between nations

questions.solution:
• Basel Convention is an international treaty that was designed to reduce movement of hazardous waste (except radioactive wastes) between nations and also to prevent the transfer of hazardous wastes from developed to developing or less developed countries.
 
• It came into force on 5 May 1992.
